references.text: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove back the sea with a strong east wind. The waters parted, and the Israelites crossed on dry ground - the same miraculous motif of parting waters.
The water stood like a wall - the same image of water standing upright, like 'a single heap' in Joshua 3:13.
The psalm describes how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back - a poetic description of the same event at the Jordan.
Fulfillment of what was predicted in verse 13 - the waters stopped and stood like a heap, and the priests stood on dry ground.
When the priests came up out of the Jordan, the water returned - confirming the miracle promised in 3:13.
Joshua explains that the Lord dried up the Jordan before them, just as he did with the Red Sea - linking the Jordan miracle to Exodus.
Elijah struck the water with his cloak, and the waters parted - the same type of water miracle at the Jordan.
Elisha struck the water, and it parted - another water-parting miracle at the Jordan.
A prophetic reference to him who dried up the sea and made the depths of the sea a road - the same God as 'the Lord of all the earth' in Joshua.
By faith they passed through the Red Sea, and the walls of Jericho fell - Hebrews mentions the power of faith in similar miracles.
